column1: # Hexplain Expression Language (HEL 1.0) conformance vectors.
# Each row is an expression, the context it is evaluated against, and what it must produce:
# a value, or an error of the given condition (specification/hel/index.html#error-conditions:
# syntax, undefined-name, forward-reference, type, range, overflow, division-by-zero, argument).
# The expected outcome is the condition, never the words of a diagnostic; an error row's sixth
# column is an informative message fragment (the reference implementation's diagnostic contains
# it, case-insensitively), which no conforming evaluator has to reproduce.
# A second implementation of HEL can run these; this one runs them on both its compiled and
# its interpreted path, so the two cannot agree with each other while disagreeing with the
# specification.
# Columns (tab-separated): name, expression, expectation (value|error), expected (a JSON
# literal; for an error, the condition as a JSON string), the context as standard base64 of
# JSON, and, for an error row only, an informative message fragment as a JSON string. The context is the CURRENT STRUCT (instance): its keys are the
# fields the struct declares, so a bare name resolves against it. A key present with the
# value null is a declared optional field that is absent (it reads as Null); a name that is
# not a key is UNDECLARED and must raise an undefined-name error. A runner therefore passes
# the context's key set as the struct's declared schema. JSON whole numbers are Integers and
# numbers with a fraction are Floats, so an integral Float cannot be written as an expected
# value; the rows avoid needing one.
# NaN has no JSON spelling, so NaN rows build it in the expression: 1e308 * 10.0 overflows to
# Infinity, and Infinity - Infinity is NaN.
# TREE CONTEXTS. A context whose only key is "$tree" is a struct-tree context, which the flat
# form cannot express. Its members: "root", the parsed tree (a JSON object is a struct node whose
# keys are its declared fields, an array an array node, null a declared field that is absent);
# "instance", the node path (Processing Model, IRI minting: root/hdr/items/1) of the current
# struct node, and "self", a node path or a JSON value for the value under test (null: undefined;
# a JSON string that is a node path of this tree, root or root/..., denotes that NODE, never the
# string, so a String value under test that spells a node path cannot be given here);
# "stream", the three stream.* integers; "param", the parameters of the instance's struct (its
# keys are the declared parameters); "unparsed", the node paths of declared fields not yet reached
# (reading one is a forward-reference error; a declared field that is null and not listed here is
# an absent optional field, Null); "extents", node path to [start, end) byte offsets for sizeof;
# and "registers", scheme IRI to the notations of its concepts, the run's register source for
# inRegister(). A runner binds instance, parent (the struct node holding the instance, by path),
# root, self, stream and param from these and evaluates as the name-binding table states.
# NOT COVERED HERE: evaluationInstant() needs a reference instant, partExtension() and asset.*
# need an asset. Bytes values (and so the Bytes-vs-String comparison rules) and uint64 values
# above 2^63-1 have no JSON spelling that survives the runner's conversion (a JSON number
# becomes a signed 64-bit Integer), so they are not covered either; the literal-range rows cover
# the part of the uint64 rule that a literal can reach. Load-time rejection of an unsupported
# extension group, and of param.<n> for a parameter the struct does not declare, is a property
# of a processor, not of one expression. Those are exercised by the engine suites; the gap is
# stated here rather than left to be inferred from absence. The processor conformance suite
# (specification/conformance/, the physical-parser cases named pp-hel-*) carries them too: its
# cases have a declaration order, nested schemas, Bytes and uint64 values, stream positions and
# asset contexts.
